input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position. Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables (20.1) and for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Standard mechanics are present (prompt notice, cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense, control of defence, prejudice-limited notice failure, and no adverse settlement without consent) (20.4), and 20.5 adds procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in addition to (not in place of) the defence obligation. Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow — unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's own violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and Vendor instructions. Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, so Vendor's indemnity is not squeezed by the liability cap (better than the fallback 3× super-cap). No redline required; separate concerns about the cap base in 21.1 belong to the limitation-of-liability rule.
